page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Daldsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance is bundled with 1890 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate exceptional single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU testing, rank in the strong top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth and multi-core stress-ng performance sit in the average range. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the processor delivers top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M parameter models and strong performance on medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32alds_v7 offers a dense compute profile with a high-frequency CPU and integrated local storage, making it highly resource-efficient for workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The lack of a GPU and the low memory-to-vCPU ratio represent clear design tradeoffs. This configuration is highly suited for high-throughput web serving, single-threaded batch processing, lightweight LLM inference, and compute-heavy applications that benefit from fast local disk access.
